questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'European Traders Arrive: The Portuguese' refers to.
questions.a: The sea route to India brought European traders to Indian shores at the end of the fifteenth century, with the Portuguese among the first to set up trading posts and forts on the coasts, opening the chapter of European rivalry for Indian trade.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'European Traders Arrive: The Portuguese'.
questions.a: Ocean routes turned India into a stage for European commercial rivalry.

questions.q: Under which section is 'European Traders Arrive: The Portuguese' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2 (source: hees102.txt lines 1-155 (arrival of the Portuguese in India))

concepts.title: The Delhi Sultanate and Its Resistance

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Delhi Sultanate and Its Resistance' refers to.
questions.a: From the thirteenth century the Delhi Sultanate ruled large parts of north India through dynasties like the Tughlaqs and Lodis, but its power faced constant resistance from regional kingdoms, and southern powers such as the Vijayanagara Empire stayed outside its grip.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Delhi Sultanate and Its Resistance'.
questions.a: Sultanate control stretched far but never unopposed - regional powers pushed back.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Delhi Sultanate and Its Resistance' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2 (source: hees102.txt lines 155-510 (sultanate dynasties, resistance, Tughlaq and Lodi extents))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Vijayanagara Empire' refers to.
questions.a: Founded in the fourteenth century in the Deccan, the Vijayanagara Empire grew into a powerful Hindu kingdom famous for its wealth, trade and the city of Hampi, standing as a major counterforce to the sultanates of the north.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Vijayanagara Empire'.
questions.a: Vijayanagara anchored southern power against northern expansion.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Vijayanagara Empire' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Rajputs, Hoysalas and Regional Kingdoms' refers to.
questions.a: Beyond the big empires, the political map was studded with regional kingdoms - Rajput houses in the north and west, the Hoysalas in the south, the Eastern Gangas in Odisha - each building temples, trade and armies and adding their patches to India's changing map.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Rajputs, Hoysalas and Regional Kingdoms'.
questions.a: Many strong regional kingdoms, not one power, made the medieval political map.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Rajputs, Hoysalas and Regional Kingdoms' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2 (source: hees102.txt lines 155-165 (Eastern Ganga and Hoysala territories), 390-445)
